newsitem.title: USA: Regional Bell marketing funds $21 billion-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Regional Bell marketing funds $21 billion-analyst.

text.p: The regional Bell telephone companies have a total of $21 billion in marketing revenue to spend on customers, Dillon Read & Co analyst William Vogel told a telecommunications industry conference.
"Part of the reason I have had such a bullish stance on the Bells really comes down to marketing intensity," said Vogel, the conference host.

Marketing executives of the eight regional Bells said at the conference that their local presence was an effective tool for retaining customers in competing with AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp, which are gearing up to compete on local telephone service.
"We feel like we can leverage our localness and history in the community to our advantage," said James Smith, vice president of local markets for U S West Communications Group.
Brian Lane, NYNEX Corp's vice president of marketing, said his company is using its detailed customer profiles to focus on high-value customers and niche markets.
"The long distance carriers have not been able to target the high-value customers," Lane said, because they do not yet have the direct contact NYNEX has with its customers.
